messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test `testAddNonComparable` attempts to add a plain Object (which is not Comparable) to an instance of Frequency via `addValue(new Object())`. The test expects an IllegalArgumentException to be thrown in this case.

Examining the code for the method `Frequency.addValue(Object v)` shows that it is deprecated and simply casts the Object to `Comparable<?>` and delegates to `addValue(Comparable<?>)`. This means any `Object` passed is unsafely cast to Comparable without a prior check.

The relevant method `Frequency.addValue(Comparable<?>)` attempts to add the Comparable `v` to a frequency table (`freqTable`). If `v` is an Integer, it converts it to a Long. Then it attempts to get the count for the object from `freqTable`. If a ClassCastException occurs during this retrieval or insertion (likely if the object is not Comparable with the existing entries), the method catches the exception and throws an IllegalArgumentException with the message "Value not comparable to existing values."

Because `addValue(Object)` blindly casts to Comparable, if a non-Comparable Object is added it leads to a runtime ClassCastException during the cast before even reaching the `addValue(Comparable<?>)` method to throw the intended IllegalArgumentException in a controlled way. Therefore the root issue is that `addValue(Object)` allows adding plain Objects by casting them to Comparable without validation. This violates the intention described in the bug report that only Comparable objects should be allowed.

Hence the bug occurs because `addValue(Object)` improperly accepts any Object but tries to treat it as Comparable without checks, leading to the test failing since the cast fails silently or leads to inconsistent behavior after the first non-Comparable insertion.

The fix should be to restrict `addValue(Object)` to accept only instances of Comparable and reject others immediately with an appropriate exception, thereby preventing invalid data from being added.

No recent bug reports are strongly relevant to this particular issue because they focus on fraction comparison or utility math methods unrelated to Frequency.

In sum, the issue is that `Frequency.addValue(Object)` method is deprecated but still present and allows unsafe casting of any Object to Comparable without validation, causing bugs when non-Comparable objects are added, as demonstrated by the failing test case.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
